item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 260531
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located well to the west of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Central East Pacific (EP93):
Shower and thunderstorm activity has increased since yesterday in
association with a tropical wave located well to the south of
southwestern Mexico. Environmental conditions are expected to
support gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression is likely to form during the next couple of days while it
moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Western East Pacific:
A weak, elongated area of low pressure located well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands is producing disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression is
likely to form late this week or early this weekend while the system
drifts to the northeast, then turns westward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form this weekend well to the south
of southwestern Mexico. Environmental conditions appear favorable
for some gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression could form by early next week while it moves westward to
west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week or over the weekend. Some gradual development
is possible by early next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Iselle (EP4/EP092026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...ISELLE DRIFTING WEST-NORTHWESTWARD... As of 2:00 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 the center of Iselle was located near 21.8, -123.5 with movement WNW at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 996 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 50 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Public Advisory Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 260836
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Iselle Advisory Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
200 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026
 
...ISELLE DRIFTING WEST-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.8N 123.5W
ABOUT 870 MI...1405 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...996 MB...29.42 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Iselle was 
located near latitude 21.8 North, longitude 123.5 West. Iselle is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected to continue over the next few days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Steady weakening is expected, and Iselle is forecast to become a 
post-tropical remnant low by early Thursday. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles (370 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 996 mb (29.42 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle will continue to affect the west
coast of the Baja California Peninsula for a couple more days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026 
592 
WTPZ44 KNHC 260838
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Iselle Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
200 AM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026
 
Moderate northerly wind shear and dry air entrainment are affecting 
Iselle this morning. An earlier GPM microwave pass indicated that 
the circulation is better established to the north and east of the 
center, with less definition on the southern and western sides. This 
structure is consistent with infrared satellite imagery, which shows 
shower and thunderstorm activity concentrated primarily northeast of 
the center. However, a recent ASCAT scatterometer pass indicated 
that winds of 40-45 kt remain present in the northeastern quadrant. 
The 0600 UTC Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was 3.0/45 kt, 
while objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 26-44 
kt. Given the scatterometer data and subjective Dvorak estimate, 
the intensity is set at 45 kt for this advisory. 

Iselle will continue on a west-northwestward heading over the next 
couple of days as a ridge builds to the north of the cyclone. 
Increasing wind shear, cooler sea surface temperatures and drier 
mid-level air will promote gradual weakening through late this week, 
and Iselle may struggle to maintain organized convection as early as 
tonight. The latest NHC forecast calls for Iselle to become 
post-tropical by 24 h and degenerate to a remnant low by 36 h. Only 
minor adjustments were made to the track and intensity forecasts for 
this advisory cycle. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  26/0900Z 21.8N 123.5W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  26/1800Z 22.2N 124.6W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  27/0600Z 22.8N 126.4W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
 36H  27/1800Z 23.5N 128.3W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 48H  28/0600Z 23.8N 130.2W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 60H  28/1800Z 24.3N 132.1W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 72H  29/0600Z...DISSIPATED
